[[File:Das Fotoalbum für Weierstraß 031 (Louis Saalschütz).jpg|thumb|Louis Saalschütz's Portrait ]]
'''Louis Saalschütz''' (1 December 1835 — 25 May 1913) was a [[Kingdom of Prussia|Prussian]]-[[Jew]]ish [[mathematician]], known for his contributions to [[number theory]] and [[mathematical analysis]].

==Biography==
 
Louis Saalschütz was born to a Jewish family in [[Königsberg]], [[Kingdom of Prussia|Prussia]], the son of [[archaeologist]] [[Joseph Levin Saalschütz]].<ref name=JE>{{Cite Jewish Encyclopedia|title=Saalschütz, Louis|url=http://www.jewishencyclopedia.com/articles/12958-saalschutz-louis|first1=Isidore|last1=Singer}}</ref> From 1854 to 1860 he studied mathematics and physics at the [[University of Königsberg]]. In 1861 he received his doctorate under the supervision of [[Franz Ernst Neumann]], with the dissertation ''Ueber die Wärmeveränderungen in den Höheren Erdschichten Unter dem Einfluss des Nicht-periodischen Temperaturwechsels an der Oberfläche''.

From 1861 to 1882 he was teacher of mathematics, mechanics, and engineering at the Royal School of Mechanics in Königsberg and the University of Königsberg, where he became an [[associate professor]] in 1875 and [[full professor]] in 1888.<ref>{{cite book|first=Reinhard|last=Bölling|editor1-first=Reinhard|editor1-last=Bölling|title=Das Fotoalbum für Weierstraß|trans-title=A Photo Album for Weierstrass|isbn=978-3-528-06602-4|language=German|publisher=Vieweg+Teubner Verlag|year=1994|page=38|doi=10.1007/978-3-322-80281-1}}</ref>

==Hypergeometric Series==
F. J. Whipple coined the phrase "Saalschützian" for generalized hypergeometric <math>_3F_2</math> series
where one of the numerator parameters is a negative integer and the sum of the denominator
parameters is one plus the sum of the numerator parameters.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=F. J. W.|last1= Whipple|title=A group of generalized hypergeometric series: relations between 120 allied series of the type F(a,b,c;e,f)|year=1925|journal=Proc. Lond. Math. Soc.|volume =s2-23|number=1|doi=10.1112/plms/s2-23.1.104|pages=104–114}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|first1=F. J. W.|last1= Whipple|title=Well-poised series and other generalized hypergeometric series|year=1926|journal=Proc. Lond. Math. Soc.|volume =s2-25|number=1|doi=10.1112/plms/s2-25.1.525|pages=525–544}}</ref> Nowadays it is also used for more general <math>_{p+1}F_p</math> series with that property.
<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Wolfgang|last1=Bühring|title=Transformation formulas for terminating Sallschützian hypergeometric series of unit argument|doi=10.1155/S1048953395000177|doi-access=free|year=1995|journal=Int. J. Stoch. Anal. |volume=8 |issue=2 |pages=189–194 }}</ref>

The "Saalschutz theorem" is
<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Louis|last1=Saalschütz|year=1890|title=Eine Summationsformel|journal=Z. Math. Physik|volume=35|pages=186–8|url=https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/id/PPN599415665_0035}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Louis|last1=Saalschütz|year=1891|title=Über einen Specialfall der hypergeometrischen Reihe dritter Ordnung|journal=Z. Math. Physik|volume=36|pages=378–295|url=https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/id/PPN599415665_0036}}</ref>

<math> _3F_2(a,b,-n;c,1+a+b-c-n;1) = \frac{(c-a)_n(c-b)_n}{(c)_n(c-a-b)_n}.</math>
